A FIXED COMPARISON

Data only · Correct physics · Wrong physics

Within each seed, these three models share their initial weights, observations, initial-condition samples and training budget. The wrong rule reverses the flow direction: v = −0.5 instead of +0.5.

Discover first. Confirm separately.

The first half of seeds are discovery runs. The second half are confirmation runs. A fixed intervention transfers the hidden features from the first discovery model trained with correct physics, resets the output layer, and retrains on confirmation observations.

A control independently scrambles each hidden input/bias column of that donor, preserving each column’s values but disrupting neuron combinations. All recipient weights remain trainable. Random initialization is the third comparison.

Same transport problem, new seeds and observation locations. Donor training adds compute; this is not evidence of reduced total cost or universal laws. Sine/cosine input features are supplied, not discovered.

Import the JSON into the Transport bridge in the updated Isomorph app. It includes initial, quarter-step and final checkpoints, weight updates, and observations.

What Isomorph adds

It recomputes metrics from the exported weights, fits neuron permutations and tanh sign flips on early-time inputs, verifies predictions are unchanged, and evaluates activation similarity on separate later-time inputs. Initial weights provide a matched baseline.

The adapter reports descriptive evidence and per-seed transfer results. It does not promote a spectral pattern or similarity score into a physical law.

What this first study controls

Truth: periodic transport, v = 0.5, D = 0.01, initial u = 0.5 + 0.4 sin(2πx). Sixteen observations at t ≤ 0.4; forecast scores at t > 0.4. The 32-neuron networks train all 161 parameters.

Known physics receives weight 0.1 in the objective. Mass conservation is measured, not enforced. Repeating a study after looking at confirmation results creates a new exploratory study; do not pool it as independent confirmation.
